title: Nvidia Is Rethinking Its Revenue-Sharing Deals with Cloud Firms
source_used: The Information, public preview paragraph of the briefing only (the article is paywalled; no other outlet carries this report). Background read at The Next Web and Tom's Hardware.
key_facts: The Information reported on Monday 5 Oct 2026 that Nvidia is reconsidering the structure of the AI Compute Partnership, an initiative it announced earlier this summer (public preview).
The program provides credit support to AI cloud providers that rent out Nvidia chips, in exchange for a cut of those rental revenues (public preview).
People involved in the discussion said Nvidia is fundamentally rethinking how the program will work (public preview).

Background, not from this report: the program was announced on 1 July 2026; on 27 Aug 2026 the Wall Street Journal reported Nvidia had put some deals on hold over antitrust and control concerns, and Nvidia said the program 'is still in place and continues to evolve' (The Next Web; Tom's Hardware).
quote_evidence: Nvidia is reconsidering the structure of an initiative it announced earlier this summer, the AI Compute Partnership, to provide credit support to AI cloud providers that rent out Nvidia chips, in exchange for a cut of those rental revenues
People involved in the discussion said Nvidia is fundamentally rethinking how the program will work.

"The new business model we introduced in July that opens up compute access to the fast-growing AI ecosystem is still in place and continues to evolve due to high demand," a spokesperson for Nvidia told Tom's Hardware.
why_it_matters_hint: A change to Nvidia's financial backing could affect the smaller AI cloud companies that rely on it to buy chips (background from The Next Web, August 2026).
event_date: The Information report of Monday 5 Oct 2026 (21:56 UTC)
notes: The Information's briefing is paywalled and no other outlet carries the story; only its public opening paragraph (the page description) was available, so the entry stays cautious. The third quote is background from Tom's Hardware (28 Aug 2026), not from this report. Treated as NEW because The Information's report of a rethink is new on 5 Oct 2026, although it continues an August story.
